Tutorials for Introduction to Modern Statistics

Source: R/ims.tutorials-package.R
ims.tutorials-package.Rd

The ims.tutorials package provides interactive tutorials covering the concepts of an introductory statistics course, worked through in R.

Details

A collection of interactive tutorials, one per chapter, accompanying Introduction to Modern Statistics by Mine Çetinkaya-Rundel and Johanna Hardin. Tutorials are built with the learnr2 package: Quarto documents rendered to static web pages. Students do the work in their own analysis.qmd, using AI, and submit evidence of each step.

Tutorials

  • Hello Data (hello-data): Chapter 1 — cases, variables, associations, and experiments versus observational studies

  • Study Design (study-design): Chapter 2 — populations and samples, four sampling methods, randomized experiments versus observational studies

  • Applications: Data (applications-data): Chapter 3 — getting to know a new dataset, and Simpson's paradox

  • Exploring Categorical Data (exploring-categorical-data): Chapter 4 — contingency tables, bar plots, conditional proportions, and comparing numerical data across groups

  • Exploring Numerical Data (exploring-numerical-data): Chapter 5 — histograms, shape, mean and standard deviation, box plots and robust statistics, transformations, and maps

  • Applications: Explore (applications-explore): Chapter 6 — keeping plots simple, color, telling a story, order, labels, and purpose

  • Linear Regression with a Single Predictor (linear-regression-single): Chapter 7 — fitting a line, residuals, correlation, least squares, R-squared, categorical predictors, and outliers

  • Linear Regression with Multiple Predictors (linear-regression-multiple): Chapter 8 — indicator and categorical predictors, multiple regression, adjusted R-squared, and stepwise model selection

  • Logistic Regression (logistic-regression): Chapter 9 — callback rates, the logit, logistic models with one and many predictors, predicted probabilities, and groups of different sizes

  • Applications: Model (applications-model): Chapter 10 — correlation, simple and multiple regression of house prices, residual plots, and backward elimination

  • Hypothesis Testing with Randomization (hypothesis-testing-randomization): Chapter 11 — hypotheses, randomization tests, null distributions, p-values, statistical discernibility

  • Confidence Intervals with Bootstrapping (confidence-intervals-bootstrap): Chapter 12 — bootstrapping, bootstrap percentile confidence intervals, confidence level

  • Inference with Mathematical Models (inference-mathematical-models): Chapter 13 — the Central Limit Theorem, the normal model, standard errors, normal-based tests and intervals

  • Decision Errors (decision-errors): Chapter 14 — two-sided tests, Type 1 and Type 2 errors, the discernibility level, power

  • Applications: Foundations (applications-foundations): Chapter 15 — the malaria vaccine case study, a randomization test, and three kinds of distribution

  • Inference for a Single Proportion (inference-for-a-single-proportion): Chapter 16 — the bootstrap test for a proportion, the success-failure condition, normal intervals and tests

  • Inference for Comparing Two Proportions (comparing-two-proportions): Chapter 17 — randomization test, bootstrap interval, and the normal model for a difference in proportions

  • Inference for Two-Way Tables (inference-two-way-tables): Chapter 18 — expected counts, the chi-squared statistic, randomization test of independence, the chi-squared distribution

  • Inference for a Single Mean (inference-single-mean): Chapter 19 — bootstrap interval for a mean, the t-distribution, t-intervals and t-tests

  • Inference for Comparing Two Independent Means (comparing-independent-means): Chapter 20 — randomization tests, bootstrap intervals, and the t-distribution for a difference in means

  • Inference for Comparing Paired Means (comparing-paired-means): Chapter 21 — paired data, randomization within pairs, bootstrap intervals, the paired t-test

  • Inference for Comparing Many Means (comparing-many-means): Chapter 22 — randomization test with the F statistic, ANOVA, the F distribution

  • Applications: Infer (applications-infer): Chapter 23 — the redundant adjectives case study: intervals and tests for one, paired, and independent means

  • Inference for Linear Regression with a Single Predictor (regression-single-inference): Chapter 24 — randomization test and bootstrap interval for a slope, the t-test and interval, model conditions

  • Inference for Linear Regression with Multiple Predictors (regression-multiple-inference): Chapter 25 — regression output with many predictors, multicollinearity, cross-validation

  • Inference for Logistic Regression (logistic-regression-inference): Chapter 26 — inference for logistic coefficients, model diagnostics, cross-validation

  • Applications: Model and Infer (applications-model-infer): Chapter 27 — the Mario Kart case study: regression output, permutation test and bootstrap for a slope, cross-validation

Running Tutorials

To run a tutorial, use: learnr2::run_tutorial(name = "tutorial_name", package = "ims.tutorials")
